title: The Crowd
author: Gustave Le Bon
blurb: A French doctor explains why sensible people turn wild in a mob — the book later studied by propagandists, marketers and dictators.

contagion.m: The spreading of a feeling or idea from person to person.
contagion.e: Laughter in a cinema spreads by contagion.

affirmation.m: A firm statement presented as true.
affirmation.e: Ads use affirmation: 'The best tea in India.'

illusions.m: False ideas or beliefs that seem real.

barbarian.e: At the match he shouted like a barbarian.

cards.title: Down the ladder
cards.text: Le Bon's key idea: a person in a crowd is not the same person alone. Joining a mob, a man drops several steps down the ladder of civilisation — he becomes impulsive, emotional and easy to lead.
cards.quote: by the mere fact that he forms part of an organised crowd, a man descends several rungs in the ladder of civilisation.
cards.qMean: In a crowd, people behave less thoughtfully than they would alone.
cards.qLife: Normally calm fans throwing bottles after their team loses.
cards.cap: The zenith of French glory; -the pinnacle of liberty · public domain

cards.title: Barbarian in a crowd
cards.text: Alone, someone may be thoughtful and educated; in a crowd, instinct takes over. Crowds feel quickly, decide quickly, and forget quickly.
cards.quote: Isolated, he may be a cultivated individual; in a crowd, he is a barbarian
cards.qMean: On your own you may be civilised; in a crowd you may act wildly.
cards.qLife: A polite colleague who joins a pile-on in a group chat.
cards.cap: The Storming of the Bastille, 1789 · public domain

cards.title: Feelings are contagious
cards.text: Emotions and actions spread through a crowd like an infection. One person panics or cheers, and soon everyone does — even against their own interests.
cards.quote: Contagion is a phenomenon of which it is easy to establish the presence
cards.qMean: Feelings spread through groups like a disease.
cards.qLife: One person runs at a sale and suddenly everyone is running.
cards.cap: Jan Brueghel the Younger - Allegory of the Tulipomania, 1640s · public domain

cards.title: Words over reasons
cards.text: Crowds don't follow arguments; they follow words and pictures. A striking slogan can move them to things none would do alone.
cards.quote: allows himself to be impressed by words and images
cards.qMean: Crowds are moved by catchy words and pictures, not by logic.
cards.qLife: A short election slogan sways more voters than a long policy paper.
cards.cap: The rioting mobs gathered in front of the Royal Palace, 9 March 1817 · public domain

cards.title: Crowds want illusions
cards.text: Masses have never wanted hard truth. They prefer comforting illusions, and whoever supplies them becomes their master.
cards.quote: The masses have never thirsted after truth.
cards.qMean: Most people prefer comforting stories to uncomfortable facts.
cards.qLife: Miracle-cure ads sell better than honest doctors' advice.
cards.cap: Honoré Daumier, crowd lithograph · public domain

cards.title: Say it, repeat it, spread it
cards.text: Leaders win crowds with three tools: bold affirmation without proof, endless repetition, and contagion — letting the idea spread on its own.
cards.qMean: Leaders persuade by stating things boldly, repeating them, and letting them spread.
cards.qLife: A jingle repeated on every channel until everyone hums it.
cards.cap: Napoleon on the Battlefield of Eylau (Antoine-Jean Gros) · public domain
